message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide on how to pull the DNS‑resolution data for **yahoo.com** from VirusTotal.  
I’ll show you the two most common ways (v3 and v2) and give you a ready‑to‑run `curl` command plus a short Python snippet.  
*(If you actually run this, replace `api_key123` with your real key – never post it in public code.)*

---

## 1. VirusTotal API v3 – “Domain” endpoint

### Endpoint
```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}
```

### Request header
```
x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

### Example `curl`

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com" | jq .
```

> *`jq .` is optional – it pretty‑prints the JSON.*

### What you’ll see

The response contains a `data` object with a `attributes` field.  
Inside `attributes` there’s a `dns_records` array that lists all the DNS records that VT has seen for the domain:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "yahoo.com",
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
      "last_analysis_date": 1700000000,
      "last_analysis_results": { ... },
      "last_dns_records": [
        {
          "type": "A",
          "value": "98.137.246.7",
          "ttl": 300,
          "timestamp": 1699999999
        },
        {
          "type": "MX",
          "value": "mx1.mail.yahoo.com",
          "priority": 10,
          "ttl": 3600,
          "timestamp": 1699999999
        },
        ...
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

> *The actual IPs, MX hosts, etc., will differ – this is just a sample.*

---

## 2. VirusTotal API v2 – “Domain Report” endpoint

If you’re still on v2, you can use:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/vtapi/v2/domain/report?domain=yahoo.com&apikey=api_key123
```

### Example `curl`

```bash
curl -s "https://www.virustotal.com/vtapi/v2/domain/report?domain=yahoo.com&apikey=api_key123" | jq .
```

### Sample output snippet

```json
{
  "domain": "yahoo.com",
  "dns_records": [
    {
      "type": "A",
      "value": "98.137.246.7",
      "ttl": 300,
      "timestamp": 1699999999
    },
    {
      "type": "MX",
      "value": "mx1.mail.yahoo.com",
      "priority": 10,
      "ttl": 3600,
      "timestamp": 1699999999
    },
    ...
  ],
  ...
}
```

---

## 3. Quick Python example (v3)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN  = "yahoo.com"
URL     = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

dns_records = data["data"]["attributes"].get("last_dns_records", [])
for rec in dns_records:
    print(f"{rec['type']} -> {rec['value']} (TTL={rec.get('ttl')})")
```

---

## Things to keep in mind

| Item | Note |
|------|------|
| **API Key** | Keep it secret. Never commit it to public repos. |
| **Rate limits** | VT v3 allows ~4 requests/minute for free accounts. |
| **Data freshness** | DNS records are cached; they may not reflect real‑time changes. |
| **Pagination** | For large domains, results may be paginated. Use `pagination` parameters if needed. |

---

### TL;DR

1. **v3** – `GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com` with header `x-apikey: api_key123`.  
2. **v2** – `GET https://www.virustotal.com/vtapi/v2/domain/report?domain=yahoo.com&apikey=api_key123`.  
3. Parse the `dns_records` (or `last_dns_records`) array to see all A, MX, TXT, etc., entries.

Run one of the `curl` commands above, and you’ll get the full list of DNS resolutions that VirusTotal has recorded for `yahoo.com`. Happy hunting!
